decisive_items: repeat imaging demonstrated reduction of free air
response.rationale: Recurrent pneumoperitoneum best fits the repeated episodes of documented free intraperitoneal air, negative laparoscopy for visceral perforation, and rapid non-surgical resolution; R4 is a close alternative but adds the unsupported qualifier 'idiopathic' when the case explicitly frames recurrence of the previous pneumoperitoneum.

rejected.why: Moyamoya disease is a listed comorbidity but has no causal link to recurrent free intraperitoneal air.
Pneumoperitoneum describes the imaging finding but omits the critical recurrent pattern established by 13 similar admissions.
Chronic intestinal pseudo-obstruction is speculative; there is no direct evidence of intestinal obstruction, and the negative laparoscopy supports pneumoperitoneum rather than pseudo-obstruction.
Familial Mediterranean fever could explain recurrent abdominal pain, but free intraperitoneal air and normal inflammatory markers on previous episodes are not characteristic.
